subject.title: fix(docs): make check:docs work in native PowerShell on Windows

question: Should maintainers fold this CRLF comparison change into the Windows command-budget and smoke fix, or keep it as a separate narrow PR after native PowerShell proof is added?
rationale: The PR has a useful narrow test/change, but it does not solve the title-level Windows docs-check problem alone and overlaps the active companion PR that carries the budget and smoke coverage work.

options.title: Fold into the Windows fix
options.body: Move the useful CRLF comparison/test into the command-budget or smoke PR so one reviewed change proves native PowerShell `check:docs` end to end.

options.title: Keep as narrow follow-up
options.body: Land this only after the body is corrected and this exact head has redacted native PowerShell `pnpm check:docs` proof showing the narrow change is still needed.

options.title: Pause if absorbed elsewhere
options.body: If the companion PR absorbs the behavior, close this branch after preserving attribution and any unique regression test value.

recommendation.title: Fold into the Windows fix
recommendation.body: Move the useful CRLF comparison/test into the command-budget or smoke PR so one reviewed change proves native PowerShell `check:docs` end to end.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across the docs formatter, Windows cmd shim, and adjacent CI workflow surface.
